bosses.name: The Lifetime Lich
bosses.pitch: Build `DynArray`, a growable array of ints, without any standard containers. The Lich feeds on leaked memory and dangling pointers.
goals: All heap memory is owned by the class (RAII): `new[]`/`delete[]` appear only inside DynArray
`push_back` grows capacity geometrically; `size()` and `capacity()` report correctly
`at(i)` throws `std::out_of_range` on a bad index; `operator[]` is unchecked
Copy constructor + copy assignment do a deep copy and survive self-assignment
Move constructor + move assignment are `noexcept` and leave the source empty but valid
A tracing switch prints every construct / copy / move / destroy (like Chapter 4's Tracer)
`main()` is a self-test: it checks every feature and returns 0 only if all checks pass
Runs clean under AddressSanitizer + UBSan (the tool builds it that way automatically)

bosses.name: The Operator Overlord
bosses.pitch: Forge `Rational<T>`, an exact fraction type that behaves like a built-in number, plus a pluggable report printer.
goals: `template <std::integral T> class Rational` — constrained with a concept
Always normalised (gcd, sign lives in the numerator); a zero denominator throws
`+ - * /`, their compound forms, unary `-`, `==` and ordering (`<=>` or `<`)
Explicit conversion to `double`; arithmetic is `constexpr` and proven with a few `static_assert`s
A user-defined literal: `3_r` gives `Rational<long long>{3, 1}`
A `ReportPrinter` interface with two implementations (aligned console table, CSV) selected at runtime
`main()` is a self-test that returns 0 only if every check passes

bosses.name: The Core Colossus
bosses.pitch: Part I finale. Build `rpn`, a reverse-Polish calculator: `./rpn 3 4 + 2 '*'` prints `14`.
goals: Tokens come from the command line (`argc`/`argv`)
A fixed-capacity `Stack<T, N>` template; overflow/underflow throw your own exception types
Operators are dispatched through a table of lambdas or function pointers, not a giant if-chain
Supports `+ - * / % ^` plus `dup`, `swap`, `drop`
Split across translation units: stack header, evaluator header/source, `main.cpp`
Clear error messages and a non-zero exit code on bad input
`./rpn --test` runs at least 10 built-in cases and returns 0 when all pass

bosses.name: The Test Golem
bosses.pitch: A bank ledger, test-driven from the first line. The Golem only falls to a green test suite.
goals: Your own micro test framework: a `TEST("name") { ... }` registration macro, `REQUIRE(expr)` reporting file:line, and a 'N passed / M failed' summary
The ledger owns accounts through `std::unique_ptr`; loggers are shared through `std::shared_ptr`
Transactions are a `std::variant<Deposit, Withdrawal, Transfer>` applied with `std::visit`
Account lookup returns `std::optional` (or a nullable pointer) and never throws
Every transaction is timestamped with `std::chrono`
Storage sits behind an interface, and the tests use a hand-written fake/mock of it
At least 12 tests, all green; `main()` returns non-zero if any test fails

bosses.name: The Container Kraken
bosses.pitch: Build `kvdb`, an in-memory key-value store with a command prompt. Commands arrive on stdin, one per line.
goals: Commands: `SET k v`, `GET k`, `DEL k`, `INCR k`, `COUNT`, `KEYS <regex>`, `HISTORY n`, `QUIT`
Storage is a `std::unordered_map`; `KEYS` output is sorted
Parsing uses `std::string_view` (no copies until a value is stored)
`KEYS` matches with `std::regex`
`HISTORY n` shows the last n commands from a bounded `std::deque`
Works in script mode: `kvdb < script.txt`
At least 3 test pairs in `tests/` (`name.in` → expected `name.out`) — the tool pipes and diffs them

files.tests/basics.in:
SET lang cpp
GET lang
GET missing
INCR hits
INCR hits
COUNT
DEL lang
DEL lang
COUNT
QUIT

readme_extra: | `INCR k` | the new integer value (missing keys start at 0) |
| `KEYS <regex>` | matching keys, sorted, one per line |
| `HISTORY n` | last n commands, oldest first |

bosses.name: The Filesystem Phantom
bosses.pitch: Build `dupes`, a duplicate-file finder. The Phantom hides copies of itself all over your disk.
goals: `dupes <dir> [--min-size N] [--ext .jpg] [--out report.txt]`
Walks recursively with `recursive_directory_iterator`, skipping symlinks and permission errors gracefully
Groups by file size first, then by a content hash (read in chunks with `ifstream`; implement FNV-1a yourself)
Report groups sorted by wasted bytes, with human-readable sizes formatted using `<iomanip>`
`--out` writes the report to a file instead of stdout
Handles a directory with 10,000+ files in a few seconds (try it on ~/Downloads)

bosses.name: The Parallel Wraith
bosses.pitch: Build `wordstorm`, a parallel word-frequency counter for a whole directory of text.
goals: A fixed-size thread pool built on your thread-safe queue from 19-3/19-4
Workers count words into per-thread maps that are merged at the end (no global lock in the hot loop)
Top-K words via `std::partial_sort`
Prints the timing for 1 thread vs N threads and the speedup
Clean shutdown; no data races under ThreadSanitizer (the tool builds it with -fsanitize=thread)
Uses at least 5 different `<algorithm>`/`<numeric>` functions in meaningful places

bosses.name: The Network Dragon
bosses.pitch: Final boss. A multi-client TCP chat server with Boost.Asio that you can connect to with `nc localhost 7777`.
goals: Async accept / read / write; any number of clients; messages broadcast to everyone else
`/nick <name>`, `/list` and `/quit` commands
Program options: `--port`, `--max-clients`, `--log-file` (Boost.ProgramOptions)
Graceful shutdown on Ctrl-C via `asio::signal_set`; all sessions are closed cleanly
`io_context` runs on a pool of worker threads, with strands where needed
Timestamped logging to a file
Demo it with three `nc` clients in three terminals

labs.task: Encrypt a file to yourself and decrypt it; make a detached signature and verify it.

labs.title: Signed git commits
labs.task: Configure git to sign your commits with your key and check them with `git log --show-signature`.

labs.title: Verify a real download
labs.task: Check a real release's signature (.sig/.asc), e.g. a GnuPG tarball, against its publisher's key.
